entries.set_purpose: One unloaded reach-and-return rehearses the retained arm path and organized standing without spending a throwing opportunity. Quiet standing replaces it only under its own comfort gate.

entries.advance_hold_reduce: Retain one listed action with the actual suitable ball/range where applicable. No added throw, fit trial or second handling attempt. A partial or failed action is counted and may require deferral; changing age is not a progression.

standard_D.variant: Unloaded Chest-Start Reach and Return — stationary bilateral teaching task
standard_D.effort_load: Unloaded, easy 1–2/10; one comfortable bilateral forward reach and return. Both feet stay planted, no dip, arch, step, jump or forced end range.
standard_D.notes: One whole counted action per set. Phase times are coaching envelopes, not a demand to rush. P2 never releases a ball; E1 attempts, including faults, use their listed opportunity. No bonus trials.

entries.set_purpose: Use the first existing main opportunity to rehearse the exact known throw on an early individual THROW cue and observe current retrieval conduct. This is one of the total 3/2/2/1 opportunities, not an extra preparation release. Known-cue instruction or a separate no-release task remains available when throwing is emerging or unavailable.
entries.prior_current_next: Actual OR-05/direct known task → first counted E0 rehearsal today → only remaining eligible E1 opportunities; no additional rehearsal precedes them.
entries.advance_hold_reduce: Keep the actual implement, feet, no-preload start, direction, easy intent and full recovery. Cap1 and compressed L use E0 only. A fault consumes E0; it is not replaced or ignored to access E1.

standard_D.variant: Stationary Two-Hand Chest Pass to Open Contained Lane — proposed teaching variation
standard_D.effort_load: Retain the actual fitted soft low-rebound ball, stance, direction and smooth quick easy release near 3/10. Planning reference 0.5 kg / 18 cm requires individual fit and inspected containment; it is not a compulsory age load. No maximal throw, distance score, new heavier ball, preload or catch. HOLD uses only comfortable support near 1–2/10.
standard_D.notes: One assigned action per set, including faults. E0 uses the first total main opportunity; E1 uses only the remaining prefix. No extra familiarization throw, test pickup or replacement response. Complete cue-specific action, waiting, retrieval and reset are detailed below. Seconds are allowances, not reaction deadlines or forced movement pace.

entries.set_purpose: Each remaining opportunity teaches one early cue interpretation while preserving the actual throw and movement demand. THROW produces one owned release; HOLD retains the ball for 3 s, parks it and waits. Both are counted. Known-cue, hold, unloaded and standing routes have their separate maintenance/instruction jobs and do not earn unobserved choice results.
entries.prior_current_next: Actual OR-05/direct stable throw and known-release/retrieval, plus current E0 → first or retained early choice in remaining OR-09 opportunities → OR-13 uses only its independently qualified movement/cue branch → OR-17 observes the actual retained rule with reduced prompting, not faster cues.
entries.advance_hold_reduce: Retain the total actual main opportunity ceiling, ball, stance, direction, intent and recovery. Default E0+E1 totals standard D3/L2, compressed D2/L1. E1 after E0 is respectively2/1/1/0, before smaller cap1/2. Select HOLD→THROW or THROW→HOLD and take only the remaining prefix; never add a cue to complete both rules. Reduce or end remaining opportunities if attention or movement deteriorates. Do not count NO-GO as a missing throw owed later.
